articles.body: 很多人把“免费”当成终点，我觉得它只是个起点；真正的门槛在后期的运维习惯。我在这台机器上跑 Python 数据分析 notebook、JupyterHub 和定时拉数脚本，半年下来，总结出的经验比参数更重要。 那些我以为会炸、结果没炸的事 开机自启这个坑，新手最容易栽。我第一次重启实例后，JupyterHub 没了，cron 任务停了，心态差点崩。后来我把所有服务都写进了 /etc/rc.local 或者用 systemd 管理。Python 脚本加 -u 参数，日志实时刷，不至于重启后黑屏半小时才发现问题。 关于备份，千万别信“云厂商会自动帮你存”。我的数据是我自己的责任。每周日深夜，脚本自动把 PostgreSQL 数据库 dump 出来，通过 rsync 推到本地 NAS。本地也没闲着，再备份一份到网盘。这套流程走了半年，只救过我一次——那次误删了配置文件，半小时找回现场。 提醒设置是最后一道防线。我在手机日历里设了三个周期：每7天的续期提醒、每月的资源盘点、每季度的数据整理。特别是续期，三丰云的免费云服务器需要手动操作，不是那种忘了就立刻回收的类型，但拖得越久风险越大。 实测中的资源真相 日常挂小任务时，1核1G真的稳如老狗。CPU 利用率长期维持在15%以下，内存常驻400MB出头。跑 JupyterHub 开几个用户笔记本，也毫无压力。 但一旦涉及数据分析的大任务，比如加载超过2GB的数据集进行预处理，内存就会吃紧。系统开始频繁交换，IO 延迟飙升。这时候加 swap 是必须的。我配置了8GB的swap文件，虽然速度远不如内存，但至少不会 OOM 杀进程。加完 swap 后，大任务平均多出30分钟的运行时间，足够完成导出。 5M 带宽在本地访问 JupyterHub 时很流畅，但如果是团队成员从外地连进来，上传下载速度就有感了。不过对于个人学习和小团队内部使用，…

articles.title: Integrar Azure Resource Health con SDK oficial: resiliencia, seguridad y modelo operativo cloud
articles.excerpt: Por qué usar SDKs oficiales en soluciones cloud nativas Cuando construimos soluciones sobre la nube, una de las primeras decisiones técnicas que aparece es cómo vamos a integrarnos con los servicios d…
articles.body: Por qué usar SDKs oficiales en soluciones cloud nativas Cuando construimos soluciones sobre la nube, una de las primeras decisiones técnicas que aparece es cómo vamos a integrarnos con los servicios del proveedor cloud. Podemos hacerlo mediante llamadas REST directas. Podemos crear nuestros propios clientes HTTP. Podemos envolver manualmente cada endpoint que necesitamos consumir. O podemos apoyarnos en los SDKs oficiales que ofrecen proveedores como Azure, AWS o Google Cloud. A primera vista, usar REST directamente puede parecer más simple. Menos dependencias, más control y una integración aparentemente más ligera.

articles.title: Cómo integrar Redis de Azure en una solución cloud nativa
articles.excerpt: Cómo integrar Redis de Azure en una solución cloud nativa Redis suele aparecer en una arquitectura como una pieza sencilla: un sitio donde guardar datos temporalmente para no repetir trabajo. Y en par…
articles.body: Cómo integrar Redis de Azure en una solución cloud nativa Redis suele aparecer en una arquitectura como una pieza sencilla: un sitio donde guardar datos temporalmente para no repetir trabajo. Y en parte es eso. Pero cuando lo llevamos a producción, Redis deja de ser simplemente una caché rápida y empieza a formar parte del modelo operativo de la solución. Afecta a la latencia, al coste, a la resiliencia, a la seguridad, a la experiencia de usuario y a la presión que ejercemos sobre bases de datos, APIs externas o servicios cloud. Por eso integrar Redis de Azure no debería consistir únicamente en copiar una cadena de conexión y hacer un GET o un SET . La integración debería responder a algunas preguntas importantes: Qué datos merece la pena cachear. Durante cuánto tiempo.
articles.author: Daniel J. Saldaña

articles.title: Cómo inventariar Service Principals en Azure y ligarlos a proyectos y repositorios
articles.excerpt: Los registros de aplicaciones, los Service Principals y las identidades administradas forman parte del día a día de cualquier plataforma que trabaje con Azure. Al principio es fácil mantenerlos bajo c…
articles.body: Los registros de aplicaciones, los Service Principals y las identidades administradas forman parte del día a día de cualquier plataforma que trabaje con Azure. Al principio es fácil mantenerlos bajo control. Hay pocos pipelines, pocas integraciones y todo el equipo recuerda para qué sirve cada identidad. Sin embargo, a medida que crece la plataforma, empiezan a aparecer preguntas difíciles de responder: ¿Qué aplicación utiliza esta identidad? ¿A qué proyecto pertenece? ¿Qué repositorio la despliega? ¿En qué entorno se usa? ¿Quién es el responsable? ¿Qué ocurre si mañana caduca uno de sus secretos? Microsoft Entra permite consultar identidades y asignar propietarios. Azure RBAC muestra qué permisos tiene cada identidad sobre los recursos de Azure.

articles.body: Un dashboard de infraestructura no aporta mucho si se limita a replicar métricas. articles.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
articles.excerpt: Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out, but if you're a sci-fi aficionado looking for similar experiences set in outer space, there are several alternatives.
articles.body: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons.

articles.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
articles.excerpt: Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey orbiter is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work by the end of November.
articles.body: Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago.

articles.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
articles.excerpt: Aldebaran looks for all the world like the brightest member of the Hyades star cluster. It isn't — and discovering why changes the way you look at constellations.
articles.body: For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth.

articles.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
articles.excerpt: A biblical mystery, an ancient Egyptian inscription and a "ring of fire" solar eclipse 3,200 years ago hold clues to when Ramesses the Great ruled.
articles.body: The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it.

articles.title: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds
articles.excerpt: A new report by the the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency discusses the threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space — including Russia, which is developing a nuke-carrying satellite.
articles.body: Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026.
